title: Moreno Urges GOP to Highlight Accomplishments as Gas Prices Hit Record High
text:
Senator Bernie Moreno urges Republicans to discuss their achievements while acknowledging voter concerns about gas prices, which remain at record highs for this time of year.
During Breitbart News's Fight Club Roundtable with Editor-in-Chief Alex Marlow and Washington Bureau Chief Matthew Boyle, Senator Bernie Moreno urged Republicans to talk more about their accomplishments while acknowledging voters' concerns about gas prices. The event took place as the national average price for regular gasoline stood at $4.41 a gallon on Thursday, October 1, down nearly seven cents from a week earlier, according to AAA. Despite the decline, prices remained at their highest level on record for this time of year.
Moreno Calls for Offense on GOP Achievements
Moreno emphasized that Republicans must go on offense and discuss the positive actions they have taken. He acknowledged that gas prices need to be lower but characterized the current situation as temporary, predicting that prices will drop once a conflict is resolved. He warned that allowing Democrats to take office would make high gas prices permanent, referencing the Biden administration as an example.
We have got to go on offense and talk about all the great things we have done, Moreno said, while also acknowledging that gas prices need to be lower, which he said there is no question about. He described the high prices as a temporary situation that will resolve itself the second that conflict is down. Gas prices will crash, he added, but if you are mad about that and if you want gas prices to go down, the last thing you should do is allow Democrats to take office, because it will make it permanently high. That is what we saw under Joe Biden, and that is what we will see under whatever lunatic comes next, he said.
September's average of $4.33 was 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83, set in 2023 during the Biden administration. The national average price for regular gasoline was $4.41 a gallon Thursday, October 1, down nearly seven cents from a week earlier, according to AAA. Despite the decline, prices remained at their highest level on record for this time of year.
Trump Administration Efforts Praised by Moreno
Moreno praised the Trump administration's work to modernize government, cut the federal workforce, combat fraud, and lower prescription drug prices, saying Republicans should talk more about those efforts. Look, we have almost 400,000 less federal workers, Moreno said. Even if you think the government is working the same as it was before, that is a massive permanent tax cut to the American people, and we can accelerate that pace of innovation. A big chunk of that is what the vice president is doing, attacking fraud, hundreds and hundreds of billions of dollars. I often hear from many, many conservatives, rightfully so. What are we doing about the debt? What are we doing about lowering the debt, lowering our debt payments? Let us get rid of fraud, he said.
The roundtable event provided a platform for Moreno to outline his views on the current political and economic landscape. He stressed the importance of communicating Republican successes to voters, particularly in areas such as government efficiency and healthcare costs. The discussion also touched on the need to address voter concerns about rising gas prices, which remain a pressing issue for many Americans.
Moreno's comments come as gas prices continue to be a focal point in political debates. The national average for regular gasoline has seen a slight decrease but remains significantly higher than in previous years. The administration's efforts to combat fraud and reduce the federal workforce are part of a broader strategy to streamline government operations and reduce costs.
Economic Context and Voter Concerns
The high gas prices are attributed to various factors, including global conflicts and supply chain issues. Moreno suggested that resolving these conflicts would lead to a drop in prices. He also criticized Democratic policies, arguing that they would lead to permanently higher gas prices. This argument aligns with broader Republican messaging ahead of upcoming elections.
The event, hosted by Breitbart News, allowed participants to interact with top leaders and ask questions. Moreno's remarks reflect ongoing Republican efforts to highlight their achievements while addressing voter anxieties about the economy. As the political landscape evolves, the debate over gas prices and government spending is likely to remain central.
